title: Self-hosted models: when running your own is worth it

videos.script: An API does four jobs for you without saying so. It holds the weights, runs them, owns the hardware, and keeps a server answering. Running your own model means taking all four. {{stack}} Start with memory, because it decides whether a model runs at all. Meta publishes the architecture, and from seven numbers you can compute every weight. Eight billion parameters at two bytes each is sixteen gigabytes. {{memory}} Store them in four bits instead and it is four. That is quantisation, and it costs some precision, which you measure on your own cases. {{speed}} Speed comes from the same memory: how fast it can be read. {{money}} Then the money. Four hundred e-mails a day cost under a dollar a month through an API. A machine would need seven hundred thousand a day to match. {{reasons}} So the reasons to run your own are rarely about cost. They are about data that may not leave, and about deciding when the model changes.
